decisions: The original Java 17 POM pins plugin versions, treats compiler warnings as fatal, runs formatter validation and static analysis, attaches sources/Javadoc, instruments tests and signs release artifacts in an explicit profile.

These are historical Maven-specific configurations. Preserve the corresponding existing Rust lint/type-check, formatting, coverage and release-artifact controls rather than adding Maven configuration to Formal AI.
A pinned plugin declaration is not runtime compatibility evidence. Historical dependency/plugin migrations and their remaining execution questions retain their earlier status.
The retained guide explains that latest labels migrate between operating system images; explicit labels avoid that migration, while installed tools and image revisions still change.

It separates GitHub/Azure availability, beta support, architecture, larger-runner labels, deprecation schedules and job-level image identity. Preserve the actual job setup metadata instead of treating a label or archive as proof of execution.

Formal AI has no active latest label or macos-14 workflow reference. Its runner-label check executes successfully across 74 files and 207 labels: macos-15, macos-15-intel, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, windows-11-arm and windows-2025.
This archived guide is historical comparison evidence, not a current external availability claim or a reason to change supported pinned labels without verification.
